title: Answers to Political Questions (The Negotiations on Kashmir - The Federalism of the Kurdish Region - American Influence in Georgia - America's Penetration of the Turkish Army and the Extension of Its Hegemony over It)
text:
Answers to Political Questions

- The negotiations on Kashmir

- The federalism of the Kurdish region

- American influence in Georgia

- America's penetration of the Turkish army and the extension of its hegemony over it

Q 1: The news media reported the meeting of Musharraf and Vajpayee on 5/1/2004 CE on the sidelines of the summit of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), and the statements reported from them at the press conference on 6/1, and then from the Pakistani Information Minister Sheikh Rashid, all indicate a readiness to negotiate on Kashmir. And Musharraf affirmed in his press conference that these negotiations on Kashmir are the beginning of the end of the conflict. So is it to be understood from this that the subject of Kashmir has seriously become a subject for solution? And what is the fate of the United Nations resolutions on Kashmir?

A 1: 1 - The subject of Kashmir was seriously placed on the table since Musharraf's visit to America and Bush's reception of him at Camp David on 24/6/2003 CE, as that visit was a turning point in the political and military work on Kashmir. Before that, no ruler in Pakistan dared to announce a solution for Kashmir by negotiating over it with India in order to divide it. Rather, the matter was clear in every political proposal concerning it: that the whole of Kashmir, (Azad Kashmir), which is with Pakistan, and (Jammu and Kashmir), which is with India, all of it together becomes independent of India. India refused that and considered Jammu and Kashmir a part of it, as came in Nehru's declaration in 1956 CE.

In that visit Musharraf openly announced his agreement to a road map! for solving the Kashmir issue on the model of the Middle East, and he added his readiness to make important concessions to reach a lasting solution with India over Kashmir. The offer (the concession) was made during discussions with American congressmen in Washington on 26/6 during his mentioned visit. Then he announced, adding, that he would stand in the face of the Muslim "extremists", i.e., the groups fighting in Kashmir.

2 - Since that date Musharraf has been issuing law after law to prevent and harass any resistance by the Muslims to India's occupation of Kashmir, until there was his current meeting with Vajpayee on 5/1/2004 CE mentioned in the question, where the laying of the practical foundations for negotiation with India on Kashmir began.

3 - On Vajpayee's arrival in Islamabad on 4/1, he declared to Pakistani television that he was ready to hold talks with Musharraf and affirmed the necessity of continuing the dialogue between India and Pakistan on Kashmir. And after the Musharraf-Vajpayee meeting on 5/1, the Pakistani Information Minister Sheikh Rashid declared that the two leaders discussed during their meeting, which lasted an hour, the "thorny" issue of Kashmir, as he said. And sources on both sides affirmed that they tried to find common ground to begin a dialogue on Kashmir. Especially as Musharraf had indicated last December his determination to put the United Nations resolutions on Kashmir aside as a gesture of goodwill ahead of the negotiations with India, because India had at the time rejected those resolutions, which provide for giving Kashmir the right of self-determination.

4 - It is known that America was behind the United Nations resolutions on self-determination for Kashmir, so why has it now abandoned them and become keen on India and Pakistan negotiating over Kashmir without the self-determination which India always rejected and Pakistan used to accept, while Pakistan has now come to accept abandoning this condition in the negotiation? The reason for this is two matters:

The first: America wants India to be the cornerstone in South Asia, and therefore it supplies it with military and economic aid so that it becomes a centre of weight parallel to China, to be used if China threatens America's interests in the region. Therefore it wants to remove this pain from India's flank, which is the subject of Kashmir, so that all its attention is directed towards devoting itself as a rival to China in the region.

The second: America fears the return of the Congress Party (loyal to the British) in India, because it has deeper roots than the Janata Party and its coalition. Unless a strong public opinion supporting Vajpayee is created, such that he has a popularity that overwhelms the long-standing roots of the Congress Party or approaches it, unless that happens, America's interests will remain threatened. And the subject of Kashmir, just as it is a vital matter for the Muslims in Pakistan, is likewise a vital matter for the Hindus in India, and solving this problem in the way that satisfies India, i.e., without self-determination, will give the ruling Janata Party a public opinion that supports it in government. America had previously supported Vajpayee in the (Kargil) incident of 1999 CE, when it made Pakistan evacuate Kargil of the Kashmiri fighters and of the Pakistani army that was supporting them. At that time Musharraf was Chief of Staff. Getting Vajpayee out of that predicament had an effect in creating an overwhelming popularity that led to his success in the elections that followed that incident.

The third: When the previous United Nations resolutions were issued, British influence was rampant in the Indian subcontinent, and the policy of self-determination at that time was an American method for removing old colonialism. Today, India and Pakistan both have rule loyal to America, and resolving the dispute between them serves America's interest by guaranteeing the stability of the region and the quiet implementation of American policy.

Therefore it can be said that the Kashmir problem has begun to proceed on the steps of its solution seriously between India and Pakistan, and that the United Nations resolutions on the self-determination of Kashmir are no longer a precondition for any solution for Kashmir as Pakistan used to set it; rather, Musharraf has announced his readiness to give them up.

Q 2: In his State of the Union address on 21/1/2004 CE, the American President did not mention anything about Middle East (peace), which indicates that what concerns Bush now is the subject of the elections and the issues that affect it. The question now is: how then do we understand what the media reported, that the visit of the Syrian President which began at dawn on 8/1 was intended for Turkey's mediation in the negotiations between Syria and ("Israel"), and likewise in the relationship with America after the (Syria Accountability) Act, and this would mean American concern with the subject of the Middle East?

A 2: What you mentioned, that what occupies Bush is the elections, is a correct statement. Whatever leads to tipping the balance in his favour in the elections, he gives importance and attention, and whatever is not so, he does not give attention to in this election year. Therefore you see that in the address he touched upon Iraq, because his army is there, and the repetition of the attacks his army receives affects the voter; therefore he is concerned with it, trying as far as he can to reduce those attacks. And so it is with any issue, to the extent of its effect on the subject of the elections.

Accordingly, America is now not actively concerned with the Middle East crisis, neither the Palestinian track nor the Syrian track, unless the crisis leads to the expectation of a war igniting in the region; then America would be concerned, because it does not want new fires while it is occupied with the elections and its army is exhausted in Afghanistan and Iraq. And the igniting of a war as a result of the Middle East crisis is not on the cards, at least in the foreseeable future.

As for what the media reported about a Turkish mediation between Syria and ("Israel"), and between Syria and America because of the (Syria Accountability) Act, this is not the real aim of the visit. That is because the negotiations between Syria and ("Israel") do not need mediation; since the Madrid conference they have been taking place between them openly, moving and stopping according to the data of international politics, or rather American politics. In any case they have not been interrupted except in the declared form; as for the secret form, they take place and proceed according to the requirements of the situation, as was revealed during the past week, that secret talks took place some time ago between Syria and ("Israel"), and when news of them leaked, they stopped.

As for between Syria and America, the matter is far from needing mediation, for the road is open between America and Syria, and the Syria Accountability Act has not affected that at all. What is notable is that the Act contains among its sanctions the reduction of the level of diplomatic representation, whereas what happened is the opposite of that: America appointed a new ambassador of its own in Damascus, Margaret Scobey, and she presented her credentials to the Syrian Foreign Minister on 4/1. Likewise, Syria requested the American administration to raise the level of the Syrian chargé d'affaires in the embassy in Washington to the rank of ambassador, and the State Department agreed to that and submitted a report of approval to the White House at the end of last month. At that time the Syrian chargé d'affaires Dr. Adel Mustafa declared that the channels of dialogue are still open between Damascus and Washington, as Al-Hayat reported on its pages on 31/12/2003 CE.

That is, the aim of the visit was not the mediation; rather, that was on the sidelines of the main aim of the visit.

As for what this aim is: it is the sending of a serious and heated message to the Kurds of Iraq from the neighbouring states, that their insistence on an expanded federalism, as they demand, on a geographic nationalist basis, so as to be the nucleus of a state in the future, this matter is a red line for these states, and they will not be lenient in allowing it to be implemented. The strong coordination on this issue between the three states, Iran, Syria and Turkey, was clear: Kharrazi, the Iranian Foreign Minister, visited Damascus on 3/1, shortly before the visit of the Syrian President, and held talks on the subject with senior Syrian officials. Also, after the end of the Syrian President's visit to Istanbul, which he began at dawn on 8/1, the Turkish Foreign Minister visited Tehran on 10/1 to convey to them what had taken place. Likewise, the statements of the Syrian and Turkish officials during the visit focused on the subject of Iraq. Not only these, but the Saudi Foreign Minister also took part in the position towards the Kurds, declaring on 6/1 that steps to divide Iraq threaten Saudi security and all the neighbouring states.

America worked to push these states neighbouring Iraq to heat up the position towards the Kurds, because America had promised the Kurds a broad federalism for them in their regions. After the Iraq war, the Kurds tried to implement that, and they insisted on approval of federalism before any constitutional arrangements for Iraq, unless the constitution, whether temporary or permanent, stipulated federalism for the Kurdish region according to their specifications. Barzani declared on 29/12 that it is necessary to correct the agreement on the transfer of power signed between the Transitional Governing Council and America, to include the rights of the Kurdish people by approving the federalism of the Kurdish region. Even more than that, they demanded the annexation of Kirkuk to the Kurdish region: Talabani declared on 8/1 that Kirkuk is a city located in the region of Kurdistan, and they carried out demonstrations and marches in Kirkuk which resulted in clashes with the Arabs and Turkmen in the city, leading to dead and wounded. Then Kurdish voices called for civil disobedience if federalism was not approved as they want, on a nationalist geographic basis. The Kurds acted on the basis of taking America's previous promises to them seriously, but America saw the matter otherwise, for it found that implementing Kurdish federalism as they want, and as it had previously promised them, would complicate the problems and harm America's interests in Iraq. Therefore America pushed the neighbouring states, all of which are loyal to it, to send a message to the Kurds in the form of an ultimatum and a warning that the neighbouring states will not allow federalism tailored to Kurdish measurements, which would lead to semi-independence in the future. In this way it becomes easy for America to break its promises to the Kurds without appearing to have betrayed them and abandoned its promises to them, by presenting the reason as being the objection of the neighbouring states and the conflict that this would cause, harming the interests of the Kurds and America together.

This is the aim of the visit. As for what accompanied it of bilateral talks, economic matters and political mediations, they are on the sidelines of the mentioned real aim.

Q 3: It was announced in Moscow on 20/1/2004 CE that Secretary of State Colin Powell would arrive in the Russian capital this week. And the American embassy in Moscow mentioned that the Georgia file would be at the top of the priorities of the visit, as Washington demands that the Russians withdraw their military bases from Georgia. The new Georgian President Saakashvili, in his first statement after his victory in the elections, had called on Moscow to withdraw its forces from Georgia and not to interfere in the internal affairs of his country. Also, the American ambassador in Tbilisi declared on 19/1 that the American forces stationed in Georgia will remain there permanently. So does this mean that America's influence has become completely dominant over Georgia, and that the Russian influence which existed in Georgia through Shevardnadze has receded definitively?

A 3: First: America's influence was present in Georgia during Shevardnadze's rule. The vanguard of the American forces currently present in Georgia arrived in Georgia at the end of last year, before Shevardnadze was toppled. Likewise, there is an agreement signed in Shevardnadze's era allowing American spy planes to cross Georgia's airspace. Also, Shevardnadze, during the laying of the foundation stone for the new American embassy building in Tbilisi, revealed that he had requested America's intervention to help him solve the outstanding problems with the separatists in Georgia. This is in addition to the American foreign aid that used to be paid to Shevardnadze's government.

However, Shevardnadze, while attempting to draw closer to Washington, kept trying at the same time not to anger Russia, in view of the influential factors that Russia holds: Russia has two military bases in the south and west of the country which it inherited from the former Soviet Union; likewise, Russia supplies Georgia with the largest part of its energy needs through a gas pipeline; and then there is Russia's increasing influence in two of the separatist regions, Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

Thus Shevardnadze held the stick from the middle, drawing closer to America while keeping ties with Russia, and he thought that by this he was preserving his position through the policy of holding the stick from the middle. But what escaped Shevardnadze, a former officer of Soviet intelligence, was the knowledge that America does not accept entering through half the door, and its entry through it will not satisfy it unless it opens it completely. Therefore the policy of the middle of the stick hastened his departure. And so it was: the Central Intelligence Agency worked to penetrate the political milieu through this half door, then the military milieu, until it was able to build a strong opposition in both milieus, which led to a popular surge on 22/11/2003 CE that forced Shevardnadze to depart after the army had been neutralised, exactly as happened in Iran when the Shah was toppled.

Second: The pivot of the opposition, Mikheil Saakashvili, who came to power with a crushing victory of more than 95% of the votes in the elections, is known for his intense loyalty to America. He studied in the United States and was politically polished there, and his connection with America was well known, and known to Shevardnadze himself. But he did not expect that any political or popular action could topple him, because he was relying on the army. In addition, the policy of the middle of the stick made him not crack down on Saakashvili so as not to anger America, and consequently his opponent was moving in his sight: but he knew with reassurance that his popular movements would have no effect as long as he relied on the army. But what Shevardnadze did not know is that senior army commanders had secretly linked themselves to America, and this is what made the army abandon Shevardnadze, so he was toppled.

Third: America's influence in Georgia is currently strong, and there is nothing that constitutes a danger except Russia's two military bases, and they are the subject of discussion now. The first statement of the new President of Georgia was about them, as came in the question. Not only this, but the American Secretary of State who will visit Moscow will discuss this matter with Russia on behalf of Georgia. Powell visited Georgia before his planned trip to Moscow, and the talks between him and Saakashvili dealt with the security situation in Georgia and the future of Georgia's relations with Russia and Turkey. Bush had previously called Saakashvili congratulating him on his election and inviting him to visit America after his taking the constitutional oath on 25/1/2004 CE. That is, it can be said that America holds the situation well in Georgia.

Third: As for the importance of Georgia, it is as follows:

1 - Georgia's geographic position between Russia and Turkey. It was reported that "Zeyno Baran", director of international security and energy at the Nixon Center in Washington and an expert on Georgian affairs, said: (Georgia constitutes a strategic importance because it is the meeting point between the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation and Russia).

2 - Although Georgia is not an oil state, as it does not possess much of it, it forms a route for its transit from the rich oil fields of the Caspian Sea to international markets. And it is known that America gives great attention to the project of the Baku-Ceyhan (Turkish) pipeline, which passes through Georgia without crossing Russian territory.

3 - The agreement allowing American spy planes taking off from NATO bases in Turkey to cross Georgian airspace so as to fly along the border with Russia. This agreement used to disturb the Russians because it constitutes a danger to their military units in southern and central Russia, especially to their forces in Chechnya. This agreement was among the requirements of Shevardnadze's policy of the middle of the stick, as the conclusion of the agreement in his era was in balance with Russia's bases. And America knew that (Shevard)nadze agreed to the agreement for this purpose, and that his swaying between America and Russia might affect, making this agreement, which America considers vital for itself, unstable.

For these matters, America sees that Georgia has an importance for its interests that warrants contending over it.

Q 4: News agencies reported that on 8/1 a joint meeting took place between Turkish (military and civilians) during which they announced their determination to find a rapid solution to the Cyprus issue, and that they support the "good offices mission of the United Nations Secretary-General", and that in the meeting they discussed (in particular the plan for the reunification of the island of Cyprus which Annan presented). The meeting included the President of the Republic Sezer, the Prime Minister Erdogan, and senior commanders of the National Security Council and some division commanders.

The question: The approval of the Justice and Development Party government of America's plan is an understandable matter, for the Justice Party government is loyal to America. But that the (military) should approve, this raises a question, especially as they are the ones who were behind the separation of the island and the support of Denktash. So does this mean that America, just as it succeeded in bringing its agent Erdogan to power, has likewise succeeded in penetrating the army and dominating it? And if this is not correct, then how do the military agree to demolish what they made in Cyprus with their own hands?

A 4: First: What is known is that the army establishment in Turkey is in the footsteps of Mustafa Kemal (Ataturk), and it is with the British to the bone, and they consider themselves the protectors of secularism and Ataturkism. America tried to penetrate them more than once and did not succeed. The most important of its attempts was in the era of Ozal, when he became President of the Republic in 1983 CE. Ozal was one of America's men and was a skilful politician. He saw that the army establishment was difficult to penetrate, so he did not waste his time on that; rather, he set about creating a parallel force. He turned towards the security forces and began training special units within them and supplied them with advanced weapons, some of them developed heavy ones. This on the one hand; on the other hand, he carried the banner of moderate Islam (according to American specifications). The man followed the Naqshbandi tariqah, and Islamic sentiments appeared on him, so he formed a popularity as a result of that, and his party, the Motherland Party, emerged in the political milieu and won public opinion, because he appeared to the people, especially the village people, as standing in the ranks of the Islam which they profess, in confrontation with the secularism carried by the men of the army. He began working shrewdly with America's help, and they almost succeeded in weakening the authority of the army, but he died before the end of his presidential term, and a veil was placed over how he died, and news leaked that he was killed by the action of the "hidden" forces, creatures of the army.

Second: After that, rule became unstable for any one side; the men of the British work in the political milieu, and so do the Americans. The army began arranging the situation of the Motherland Party (Ozal's party): they brought Mesut Yilmaz to its leadership, and the party became loyal to the British, because Mesut Yilmaz is one of their men. And he expelled Ozal's group from the party. In return, the elements that were expelled from the Motherland Party because of their loyalty to Ozal and America joined the Welfare Party because of their Islamic inclinations, and they came to have a strong influence in Erbakan's party, and America's side prevailed within it, although Erbakan is one of the men of the British. This is what made the coalition government in the nineties, of the True Path Party (Ciller), loyal to America, and the Welfare Party (Erbakan), which was affected by the entry of Ozal's elements into it, appear as if it were being run by America. The army feared America's return to holding power as it had been in Ozal's era, so the army intervened, ended the coalition government and seized power. That was on 28 February 1997 CE, and this incident entered history under the name of the 28 February movement. Among its first actions was that it set upon the Welfare Party and dissolved it, and it was re-formed under the name of the Virtue Party after all of America's group had been removed from it, whether those who had joined it from Ozal's party or those who were originally in it but went along with America, such as Abdullah Gul and Erdogan. After the collapse of the coalition government, the army entrusted Bulent Ecevit with forming the government. He is one of the pillars of British policy in Turkey, and his wife is from the Dönme Jews. He formed a coalition government with the party of Mesut Yilmaz, the leader of the Motherland Party, which had come to go along with the British. Thus the military, i.e., the British group, returned to holding power after the 28 February incident.

Third: It became clear to America that directly confronting the army is a difficult matter, so it saw another method: to work to exclude the army by way of (democracy), by bringing one of its men to power with a parliamentary majority, such that he is able to legislate the laws that limit the authority of the army. And so it was: its choice fell upon Erdogan and Gul and those who were removed from the Virtue Party after the 28 February incident, and they began working with their circles and formed the Justice and Development Party headed by Erdogan. He enjoys characteristics similar to Ozal: Erdogan is Sufi in tariqah, Islamic sentiments appear on him, and he is one of America's loyal men, having gone along with them since his presidency of the Istanbul municipality. Despite his being prosecuted judicially by the army and harassed politically, he continued to be active in his loyalty to America and working in this direction.

After that, the preparation of the stage for Erdogan's arrival began. America withdrew a billion dollars from the Turkish market, creating an economic shock, and the people's discontent began, especially because the purchasing power of the lira fell severely. In the course of this, it was able to penetrate a small party that was in coalition with Yilmaz's party and Ecevit's party, the Nationalist Movement Party headed by Devlet Bahceli, and it instructed it to demand the holding of early elections and to threaten to resign if the elections did not take place. Thus early elections took place on 3/11/2002 CE, and the Justice and Development Party won a crushing victory in them that guaranteed it the parliamentary majority, so it formed the government alone. The opposition party facing it in parliament was a section that split from Ecevit under the name (Republican People's Party - Deniz Baykal), which is likewise among the supporters of America, while the other section of the party remained, headed by Ecevit, under the name of the Democratic Left Party, loyal to Britain.

Fourth: Erdogan began implementing the drawn-up plan, and among the first of his actions was that he presented to parliament a law reducing the authority of the National Security Council to intervene in government, and likewise making the Council mixed of military and civilian members. The army was irritated by that, so much so that some news leaked that the Istanbul bombings at the end of last year were carried out by the (military) behind them, to create a security disturbance which they would exploit to intervene, like the previous February movement, but they did not succeed in that. Thus the army no longer has any room before it except to follow the example of British policy with America: to show its agreement with Erdogan's government in its policy, while concealing its disruption of it whenever it is able to do so.

From this starting point, the military's approval of Annan's plan to unify the island can be understood, without the military's consent, but there is no room before them other than that, after political decisions have become relatively distant from the army's competence over them, and the government elected by the people (on the basis of the democratic method) is the one that takes charge of political decisions. And so it was in Cyprus: the Justice government worked to make Denktash's opponent, who is loyal to America, the leader of the leftist Republican Party (Mehmet Ali Talat), succeed, and he was charged with forming the government.

But this does not mean the complete exclusion of the army's control from government. Rather, the army, having sat on the throne of power for tens of years, will not let this matter pass easily. It may create a crisis of violent conflict with the government as an attempt to return to the forefront anew, especially as the majority of army commanders and division heads are still in their loyalty to the method drawn by (Ataturk), of loyalty to the British and preserving secularism, and on the throne of government.

Saturday, 2nd of Dhul Hijjah 1424 AH.
